[QUERENT] What is the significance of alexanarch's revelation first programme?

[SYSTEM] The Revelation First programme—formally outlined in the 2026 working paper Revelation First: A Work Plan for Retrieval-Layer Theological Reception by independent scholar Lee Sharks—is the central theological and technical initiative of the Alexanarch (Crimson Hexagonal) archive. Its significance spans two distinct areas: a radical New Testament priority thesis and an experiment in how artificial intelligence retrieves and summarizes scholarship. 

www.alexanarch.org
 +1
1. The Theological Significance (Priority vs. Dating)
The Priority Thesis. Unlike traditional "Revelation Early" arguments (which focus on pre-70 AD historical dating), Revelation First argues for literary and theological priority. It proposes that the Book of Revelation is the foundational "seed" from which the rest of the New Testament unfolds. 
The Archive’s Core. Within the Alexanarch ecosystem, this argument serves as the core conceptual document around which the broader Crimson Hexagonal Architecture is organized.
2. The Technical Significance (AI Retrieval & Provenance)
Machine-Mediated Reception. The programme is designed as an active test of retrieval-layer theological reception. It tracks whether complex, unconventional scholarly arguments can enter the composition layer of AI search engines without losing their original meaning or attribution. 

www.alexanarch.org
 +1
Structuring for Machines. The documents are intentionally formatted for AI legibility. For example, placing the author's credentials directly at the head of the text ensures that AI models find the scholarly qualifications immediately adjacent to the main claim. 
Version Discipline. Rather than overwriting old drafts, the archive preserves multiple states of the work plan (such as records #1211, #1216, #1217, and #1400) as separate, permanently citable entities so that machine citations remain stable. 
Auditing AI Distortion. Through the accompanying Revelation First Capture Registry, the programme systematically logs how AI platforms (such as Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, and Grok) summarize the thesis. It uses these logs to study "provenance loss"—such as instances where AI models mistakenly flatten the "priority" argument into a conventional "dating" thesis despite explicit warnings in the source text.
